newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Indonesian plan aims to reduce maternal mortality.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian plan aims to reduce maternal mortality.

text.p: Indonesia has launched a five-year plan to reduce maternal mortality by 50 percent by 1999, an Indonesian delegate at a conference on maternal mortality said on Tuesday.

"Indonesia, which has one of the highest maternal mortality rates in Asia, set a target to reduce the rate by 50 percent to 225 per 100,000 live births by end of the century," Dr Poedji Rochjati told Reuters.
Eighty percent of Indonesia's 200 million people live in rural areas. The maternal mortality rate varied from 130 to 750 per 100,000 live births in different provinces in 1994, she said.

The first world conference on maternal mortality has brought together more than 750 doctors and medical experts from 76 countries, including 13 delegations from Asia, in the southern Moroccan city of Marrakesh.
The five-day gathering aims to alert the world community to what it describes as the tragedy of one million women who die at childbirth every year due to lack of medical care.

In 1994 Indonesia, whose people live on several thousand islands, launched a policy of providing "one midwife for one village" to increase access to antenatal care to 80 percent of women nationwide from 50 percent, Rochjati said.
Seventy-nine percent of births take place at home and midwives are the first delivery assistance sought in Indonesia's rural areas.

Rochjati, a specialist at the Obstetric and Gynecology department at Soetomo hospital in Java, said maternal mortality had decreased in the first three years of government programme, but did not give a figure.
The main causes of maternal mortlity in the country are haemorrhage, infections and unsafe childbirth environment.

Asked about the feasability of the Indonesian programme, Dr Kusum Walujkar of Kolhapur hospital in India said: "Indonesia's ambitious programme can meet its target if villagers were provided with minimum health care and training...We came from Asia to discuss each other's projects and ideas in order to focus the world attention on this tragedy."
